title: Interleaved Capacity Smoothing & Triage Retreat
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:

Our current cycle commits show recurring mid-cycle scope churn caused by uneven staffing ripples across interleaved initiatives. This results in: missed ship dates for low-latency infra items, last-minute scope cuts that reduce user-value, and ad-hoc staff reassignments that increase context-switch overhead.

Goal:
- Create an operational pattern (a short playbook + decision catalog) for the start-of-cycle "Triage Retreat" that produces a stable, resilient plan: prioritized slices, guarded critical paths, and a small list of explicit fallback tranches. The output should make mid-cycle tradeoffs predictable and minimize emergency staff moves.

Scope:
- Focus on product-management + eng + design alignment for 2-week and 6-week cycles.
- Produce a checklist, a decision matrix for scope cuts, and a staffing-confidence signal that integrates with the Cycle Planner dashboard.
- Exclude hiring or headcount changes; those decisions live in People Ops.

Proposal summary:
1) Pre-retreat signals: PMs submit commit-level confidence (High/Med/Low) and top-3 risks per initiative. Engineering provides velocity risk flags and cross-team dependency map.
2) 1-day Triage Retreat workshop: facilitated 90-minute alignment for interleaved initiatives, followed by a public triage log entry and explicit fallback tranches (A/B/C).
3) Output artifacts: trimmed scope list (what to drop first), guarded goals list (must-deliver items), staff-fence rules (who cannot be reallocated without approval), and a short-run communication template for stakeholders.
4) Integration: the playbook will populate Cycle Planner UI with the fallback tranche and surfaced confidence; operations will enforce staff-fence exceptions via a lightweight approval flow.

Why this is different from prior runbooks:
- Emphasis on an explicit, ranked "trim decision catalog" keyed to customer value and latency/cost SLO impact rather than arbitrary task size.
- Staff-fence concept: minimal friction approvals for reassignments to prevent phantom rebalancing.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Workshop becomes a megameeting and generates more consensus friction than clarity. Mitigation: strict facilitation script, 90 minute timebox, and pre-read templates.
- Risk: Teams game the confidence signals. Mitigation: correlate with historical delivery variance; require two data points (PM + Eng) for High confidence.

Deliverables:
- Playbook doc (Confluence),
- Trim decision catalog (spreadsheet + mapping to OKRs),
- Starter templates for the Cycle Planner UI integration,
- One pilot run and retro notes.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook published with step-by-step facilitator script and pre-read templates
Trim decision catalog created and linked to at least 3 active initiatives and mapped to OKR metrics
Cycle Planner has a UI hook (fallback tranche + confidence) and a pilot meta-entry for at least one cycle
success_metrics: Reduction in mid-cycle unplanned scope drops by 40% for pilot initiatives (measured over two cycles)
<20% of high-confidence items reclassified mid-cycle without documented approvals
Average number of cross-team staff reassignments per cycle decreases by 30%
decisions: Use a three-tranche fallback model (Primary, Fallback-1, Fallback-2) rather than binary keep/drop
Staff-fence exceptions require PM+Tech lead sign-off and one rotation-committee approval for >2 engineers moved
Confidence signal will be a combined PM/Eng value; if they disagree, Conservatively pick the lower confidence
work_items: Design trim-decision spreadsheet schema and mapping to OKRs (owner: Mariana - Design)
Engineering: add UI hook to Cycle Planner for fallback tranche + confidence (ENG-30712)
Legal/Trust: confirm no policy blockers for staff-fence approval traces (owner: Priya - Legal)
Pilot coordination: schedule Triage Retreat for pilot initiatives in 2026-W10
